The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Late Sham T. @ Shyam T. @ Shyamasundar, in the road traffic accident that took place on 27.09.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 27.09.2023 at about 20.00 hrs., when the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EY-6467, on the left side of NH-150A Road towards Mayasandra village, and when he reached opposite to Dharmanna Bhukti Mane,
Chunchanahalli Palya, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B- 3176 by driving it in a rash and negligent and zig zag manner, dashed against the vehicle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.

It is contended that, post-mortem was conducted at Adichunchanagri hospital and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was working at Adhichunchanagiri University, B.G. Nagar as a Officer clerk and drawing a salary of Rs.40,000/- p.m.
Deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-B-3176.

Hence,
the 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have entered appearance through their learned counsels and the 2 nd respondent filed objection statement.
Inspite of giving opportunity, 1st respondent has not filed objection statement.

sentences.text: 5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B-3176 and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B-3176 was not holding valid driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident and hence, it is not liable to pay the compensation.
It is contended that Section 158(6) and 134(c) of M.V. Act are not complied by the jurisdictional police and the insured of the offending vehicle.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of deceased Sri. Late Sham T. @ Shyam T. @ Shyamasundar?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that on 27.09.2023 at about 20.00 hrs., when the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EY-6467, on the left side of NH-150A Road and when he reached opposite to Dharmanna Bhukti Mane,
Chunchanahalli Palya, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B- 3176 by driving it in a rash and negligent and zig zag manner, dashed against the vehicle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot as alleged by the petitioners?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P1 to 14.
Also examined one witness as PW.2 and he got marked the documents at Ex.P15 to 18.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.3 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 ...

As per final order For the following:

4 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 :

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 is stated to be the wife, petitioners No. 2 is stated to be minor son and petitioners No.2 and 4 are mother and father/parents of the deceased.

To prove the same,
petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased, as well as petitioners No.1 to 4 marked at Ex's.P.9 to 13 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 27.09.2023 at about 20.00 hrs., when the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EY-6467, on the left side of NH-150A Road towards Mayasandra village, and when he reached opposite to Dharmanna Bhukti Mane,
Chunchanahalli Palya, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B- 3176 by driving it in a rash and negligent and zig zag manner, dashed against the vehicle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
It is specifically urged that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

The 1st petitioner in addition to her oral testimony, got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Inquest report and statement of relatives, Spot Mahazar, Seizure mahazar, IMV Report,
P.M. Report and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any evidence to prove their defence.
12. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Bolero goods vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

sentences.text: Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners, the accident happened on NH-150A Road opposite to Dharmanna Bhukti Mane, Chunchanahalli Palya, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-B-3176 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the deceased's motor cycle a caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P2.
Ex.P1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P4 being the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of Ex.P3 along with sketch it reflects that deceased was proceeding on his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the offending vehicle came from opposite towards extreme right side of the road and hit against the deceased's Motorcycle due to which deceased fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
14. The counsel of Respondent No.1 has cross-examined PW.1 at length but nothing to be elicited from her mouth, to disbelieve the evidence of this witness.
If the driver of Bolero goods vehicle had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle and also traffic rules, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P.6 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the offending vehicle.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.4 & 6 coupled with Ex.P.8 charge sheet and also evidence of the Pw1 it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving by the Bolero goods vehicle driver.

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/
s Satbir and others
which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319

. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the Bolero goods vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Bolero goods vehicle and he was charge sheeted.

16. Further though PW1 waw cross examined by the respondent counsel at length, nothing was elicited from their mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P4 and 6 coupled with Ex.P8 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion made supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-B-3176 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Late Sham T.
@ Shyam T. @ Shyamasundar, was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-B-3176.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.
18. The petitioners have contended that the deceased was aged 44 years at the time of accident.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P9 which shows the date of birth as 26.03.1979.
The accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 44 years.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, considering the age of the deceased, the multiplier applicable to the age of 44 years is 14.
19.

Petitioners have contended that, the deceased was working at Adhichunchanagiri University,
B.G. Nagar as a Office clerk and drawing a salary of Rs.40,000/- p.m.,
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.

In order to prove the same, PW.1 has examined the office superintendent of Adichunchanagiri University as PW.2 and he has produced appointment letter, Office order, Salary slips from April 2023 to September 2023 and attendance register.
20 . The documents produced by the petitioners, as well as PW.2 depicts that deceased was permanent employee of the university and he was working in the said organization from 01.02.2016.

As per Ex.P14 and Ex.P17, the gross salary of the deceased for the month of October, November and December 2021 respectively was Rs.30,284/- and after deductions net salary was Rs.27,440/- and Anusha T P vs Jaya Pala on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148931929/
7 he does not come under income tax slab for deduction of income tax.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, this court has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.27,440/- p.m.
21.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 50%, 40 years to 50 years 30% and 50 to 60 years 15%.
The deceased is a permanent Employee and a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 44 years.
Therefore, in this case, 30% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Hence,
if 30% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.35,672/- p.m.(Rs.27,440/- +
8,232/- i.e. 30%)
The deceased died leaving behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.26,754/- p.m.(Rs.35,672 - Rs.8,918 = Rs.26,754/-).
22.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.26,754/- p.m. and the multiplier '14' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.44,94,672/- (Rs.26,754 X 12 X 14).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.44,94,672/- under the head of loss of dependency.

23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 is minor son, petitioners No.3 and 4 are the mother and father of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father, as well as Petitioner No.3 and 4 towards their deceased son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.47,03,672/-.
26.

As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1 st petitioner is the widow, petitioners No.2 is the minor son and the petitioner No.3 & 4 are the mother and father of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 40:20:20:20.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-B-3176.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.47,03,672/-(Rupees Forty Seven lakhs three thousand six hundred and seventy two only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 40%
 Petitioner No.2 - 20%
 Petitioner No.3 - 20%
 Petitioner No.4 - 20%
Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioners No.3 and 4 is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
s Satbir and others
which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319
. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.
Even in the instant case the driver of the Bolero goods vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Bolero goods vehicle and he was charge sheeted.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 44 years.
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.
The deceased is a permanent Employee and a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 44 years.
Therefore, in this case, 30% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 is minor son, petitioners No.3 and 4 are the mother and father of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father, as well as Petitioner No.3 and 4 towards their deceased son.

9 ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.47,03,672/-(Rupees Forty Seven lakhs three thousand six hundred and seventy two only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 40%
 Petitioner No.2 - 20%
 Petitioner No.3 - 20%
 Petitioner No.4 - 20%
Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioners No.3 and 4 is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
